b2019-1.ask: Carrie started a cat drawing and added more lines with her pen. Which picture could be her finished drawing?
steps: She only ADDED lines. Everything in her first drawing must still be there, exactly the same.
Check each picture: are the ears, the nose and everything she drew at the start still there unchanged?
Cross out any picture where part of the start drawing is missing or changed.
Only picture B keeps everything from the start drawing.
b2019-1.check: Lay the start drawing over B: every line matches, and B just has extras. ✓
b2019-1.spot: 'Added to' a picture? Everything old must still be there.
b2019-1.oops: Picking the nicest-looking cat instead of checking the original parts.

b2019-2.ask: Mayans wrote numbers with dots (1) and bars (5). How did they write 17?
steps: Use as many bars (5s) as fit: 3 bars = 15.
17 − 15 = 2 left over: 2 dots.
So 17 = 3 bars and 2 dots.
b2019-2.spot: Big pieces and small pieces? Use the big ones first, then fill in.

b2019-3.ask: The clock shows 20:19. What's the next time it shows the same four digits (2, 0, 1, 9)?
steps: Times go forwards. After 20:19, try to rearrange the digits into the next time.
Minutes can only go up to 59, and hours up to 23.
20:91 isn't a real time (91 minutes). 21:09 is real, and it's the next one after 20:19.
Times earlier than 20:19 (like 09:21) only come the next day, after 21:09.
b2019-3.check: 21:09 uses 2, 1, 0, 9 ✓, and no time between 20:19 and 21:09 uses those digits. ✓
b2019-3.spot: Clock puzzles? Remember minutes stop at 59 and hours at 23.
b2019-3.oops: Picking 20:91 without checking it's a real time.

b2019-4.ask: 14 girls and 12 boys. Half the class goes for a walk. At least how many are girls?
steps: Half of 26 children = 13 go.
Unluckiest case: as many boys as possible go. All 12 boys could go.
13 − 12 = 1 girl at least.
b2019-4.spot: 'At least'? Fill up with the other group as much as possible first.
b2019-4.oops: Thinking half the girls must go.

b2019-5.ask: On a real die, opposite faces add to 7. Which picture could be a real die?
steps: Opposite pairs: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4.
Faces you can see together are next to each other, never opposite.
So in a real die, no two faces you can see add up to 7.
Check each picture: only E has no two visible faces that add to 7.
b2019-5.check: In the other pictures you can find two visible faces like 2 and 5 or 3 and 4. ✓
b2019-5.spot: Dice? Opposite faces add to 7, so faces side by side never do.
b2019-5.oops: Only looking at one pair of faces.

b2019-6.ask: Which shape is NOT in the tiling design?
steps: Look carefully at the design and find each shape.
You can find triangles, squares, hexagons and big 12-sided shapes.
Look for an 8-sided shape: there isn't one.
So the octagon is the missing shape.
b2019-6.check: Count the sides of each shape in the design: 3, 4, 6 and 12, never 8. ✓
b2019-6.spot: Finding shapes? Count the sides of each one.
b2019-6.oops: Mistaking a 12-sided shape for an octagon.

b2019-7.ask: How many 2 × 2 squares can Laura colour in this cross-like figure?
steps: Look for every spot where a 2 × 2 block fits completely inside the figure.
There's one in each of the 4 corner blocks.
The middle part is a 3 × 3 square, and a 3 × 3 square holds 4 different 2 × 2 squares.
b2019-7.check: List them: 4 corners and 4 overlapping in the middle. ✓
b2019-7.spot: Counting squares inside shapes? Count in groups: corners, then the middle.
b2019-7.oops: Forgetting that 2 × 2 squares can overlap in the middle.

b2019-8.ask: A die has 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Toni throws it 3 times and adds. Which sum is impossible?
steps: Every face is odd.
Odd + odd = even. Even + odd = odd. So three odd numbers always make an ODD sum.
20 is even, so it can never be the sum.
b2019-8.spot: All odd numbers? Think odd and even instead of exact sums.
b2019-8.oops: Trying to find 20 for a long time.

b2019-9.ask: A group of kangaroos' ages add to 36. In two years they'll add to 60. How many kangaroos?
steps: In 2 years, the total grows by 60 − 36 = 24.
That's 12 per year.
Each kangaroo adds 1 year per year, so there are 12 kangaroos.
b2019-9.spot: Ages added together? The total grows by the number of people each year.

b2019-10.ask: Solids are built from equal cubes, each with a base of 8 cubes. Which one needs the most paint?
steps: Paint covers the outside. Count the little outside squares on each solid.
From below, the left, the top and the right, every solid shows 8 squares each. Those don't help you choose.
From the front and back, B shows only 3 squares each; the others show 4 each.
Solid A also has 2 squares tucked inside a gap that you can't see from any direction. Totals: A 42, B 38, the rest 40. A needs the most paint.
b2019-10.spot: Paint or surface area? Count every face that's on the outside.
b2019-10.oops: Thinking the solid with the most cubes needs the most paint.

b2019-12.ask: Riri usually eats 5 spiders a day, 10 when very hungry. She ate 60 in 9 days. How many very hungry days?
steps: If every day were normal: 9 × 5 = 45 spiders.
She ate 60, so 60 − 45 = 15 extra.
Each hungry day adds 5 extra spiders: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 days.
b2019-12.spot: Two kinds of days? Pretend they're all the normal kind, then count the extras.

b2019-13.ask: A folding yardstick has 10 parts joined in a line. Which shape can't be made with it?
steps: The yardstick is one long chain with two ends. You can fold it at the joints but not branch it.
Where three or four parts meet at a point, the chain must start or end there (it can't split).
A chain has only 2 ends. Look at each shape and count the points where an odd number of parts meet.
Shape C has too many of those points: it would need more than 2 ends.
b2019-13.check: Try tracing each shape in one line without lifting your finger or going over a part twice. C can't be done. ✓
b2019-13.spot: Can it be drawn in one line? Count the points where an odd number of lines meet.
b2019-13.oops: Only counting the parts (10) without checking how they join.

b2019-15.ask: A big triangle is divided into smaller equal-sided triangles. The small gray one has sides of 1 m. What's the big triangle's perimeter?
steps: The big triangle's corners are corners of equilateral triangles, so the big triangle is equilateral too: all its sides are equal.
Two equilateral triangles that share a side are the same size. So the small triangles touching the gray one all have 1 m sides.
Two of those 1 m sides make one side of a bigger triangle: 2 m. Its neighbours that share sides are 2 m too.
The bottom side is 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 m, so the perimeter is 3 × 5 = 15 m.
b2019-15.check: Check another side the same way: also 5 m. ✓
b2019-15.spot: Equilateral triangles? Every side is the same, so pass lengths from one triangle to the next.
b2019-15.oops: Guessing the sizes from the picture.

b2019-16.ask: 30 animals: dogs, cats, mice. The witch turns 6 dogs into cats, then 5 cats into mice. Now there are equal numbers of each. How many cats were there at the start?
steps: At the end: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 dogs, 10 cats, 10 mice.
Rewind the last step: 5 mice go back to being cats. Cats 15, mice 5.
Rewind the first step: 6 cats go back to being dogs. Cats 15 − 6 = 9, dogs 16.
At the start: 9 cats.
b2019-16.check: Start 16 dogs, 9 cats, 5 mice. 6 dogs → cats: 10, 15, 5. 5 cats → mice: 10, 10, 10. ✓
b2019-16.spot: Things change, and you know the end? Rewind.
b2019-16.oops: Undoing the steps in the wrong order.

b2019-18.ask: A square sheet is folded twice and then cut twice. How many pieces?
steps: After folding twice there are 4 layers.
Each cut goes through all 4 layers. Unfold one fold at a time and mirror the cuts.
When you unfold, the two cuts become a grid of lines across the whole square.
Those lines cut the square into 9 pieces.
b2019-18.check: Try it with paper! Fold twice, make the two cuts, unfold, count. ✓
b2019-18.spot: Folding and cutting? Unfold step by step and draw where the cuts land.
b2019-18.oops: Multiplying 4 layers × 2 cuts or similar without drawing it.

b2019-19.ask: If Alex has no hat, Bob wears one. If Bob has no hat, Carl wears one. Today Bob has no hat. Who's wearing a hat?
steps: Bob has no hat. The second rule says: then Carl wears a hat.
First rule: if Alex had no hat, Bob would wear one. But Bob doesn't.
So Alex can't be hatless: Alex wears a hat.
Both Alex and Carl wear hats.
b2019-19.check: Alex hat, Bob none, Carl hat: both rules are kept. ✓
b2019-19.spot: If-then rules? Also think backwards: if the 'then' part didn't happen, the 'if' part didn't either.
b2019-19.oops: Only using the second rule and missing what it says about Alex.

b2019-20.ask: Each net folds into a cube with a line drawn on it. On which cube does the line join up into a closed loop?
steps: When a net folds into a cube, pairs of edges join up. Label each outside edge so that edges with the same label meet.
The line on each net has two ends, each at the middle of an edge.
The line closes only if both ends are on edges with the SAME label, so they meet when folded.
Only in net D do both ends land on matching edges.
b2019-20.check: Copy net D on paper, fold it into a cube: the line is one closed loop. ✓
b2019-20.spot: Lines on nets? Mark which edges meet when folded.
b2019-20.oops: Checking the line looks connected on the flat net. It's the folded cube that matters.

b2019-21.ask: Each face of a cube has a positive whole number. Opposite faces multiply to the same product. You can see 10, 15 and 5. What's the smallest total of all six?
steps: The product (same for every pair) must be a multiple of 10, 15 and 5, because each of those is one number in a pair.
The smallest such product is 30.
b2019-21.check: 10 × 3 = 15 × 2 = 5 × 6 = 30. ✓ A bigger product like 60 makes the hidden numbers bigger.
b2019-21.spot: Equal products? Find the smallest number that all the known ones divide into.

b2019-22.ask: Six black beads and three white beads are on two balance scales. What do all nine weigh?
steps: Look at the second scale: 3 black + 1 white on one side, 1 black + 30 g on the other.
Take one black bead off each side: 2 black + 1 white = 30 g.
All the beads are 6 black + 3 white, which is three groups of (2 black + 1 white).
b2019-22.check: However much each bead weighs, three groups of 30 g is 90 g. ✓
b2019-22.spot: Balance scales? Take the same thing off both sides, then look for groups.
b2019-22.oops: Trying to find each bead's weight. You don't need it.

b2019-23.ask: Robert made 5 statements about his children. Exactly one is false. Which?
steps: Basil has 3 sisters and Ann has 2 sisters: that fits 3 daughters (Ann + 2 others).
Ann has 2 brothers means 2 sons. But then Basil (a son) would have only 1 brother, not 2.
So 'Ann has 2 brothers' and 'Basil has 2 brothers' can't both be true. One of them is the false one.
With 3 daughters and 2 sons he has 5 children, which matches statement E. So D is false.
b2019-23.check: 3 daughters + 2 sons: A ✓, B ✓, C ✓, E ✓, D ✗. Exactly one false. ✓
b2019-23.spot: Exactly one false? Look for two statements that clash.
b2019-23.oops: Forgetting a person isn't their own brother or sister.

b2019-25.ask: A cardboard net folds into a 2 × 1 × 1 box. Which picture does NOT show this box?
steps: Fold the net: keep the row with two black squares facing you, fold the row below it back, and the next row goes to the back.
The two gray squares at the top become the box's top face. That's the box in picture A.
Turn the box toward you to see C, D and E.
B shows a long face made of two white squares, but no two white squares in the net can join into one face. So B is impossible.
b2019-25.check: The other four pictures each match the folded box from some side. ✓
b2019-25.spot: Which view is impossible? Look for neighbours that can't be neighbours.
b2019-25.oops: Checking only one face of each picture.

b2019-26.ask: Emily's 8 cousins each appear in 2 or 3 selfies. Every selfie has exactly 5 cousins. How many selfies?
steps: Count 'cousin appearances'. Each cousin is in 2 or 3 pictures, so the total is between 8 × 2 = 16 and 8 × 3 = 24.
Each selfie has 5 cousins, so the total is a multiple of 5.
The only multiple of 5 between 16 and 24 is 20.
20 ÷ 5 = 4 selfies.
b2019-26.check: 4 pictures × 5 = 20 appearances. 4 cousins in 3 pictures + 4 cousins in 2 = 12 + 8 = 20. ✓
b2019-26.spot: Counting the same thing two ways? Count appearances by person and by picture.

b2019-27.ask: Two identical pyramids of 15 numbered cans. Jette knocks down 6 cans worth 25 points. Willi knocks down 4 cans. How many points does Willi get?
steps: Add up the cans still standing after Jette: 9 + 4 + 5 + 8 + 6 + 1 + 9 + 7 + 6 = 55.
All 15 cans together: 55 + 25 = 80 points.
Add up the cans still standing after Willi: 54.
Willi knocked down 80 − 54 = 26 points.
b2019-27.spot: Two pictures of the same thing? Use one to find the total, then compare.
b2019-27.oops: Trying to work out which cans Willi hit.

b2019-28.ask: Every digit on the clock has the same two segments broken. It shows a broken time. What will it show 3 hours 45 minutes later?
steps: Compare the broken digits with the full digits 0 to 9. Find which two segments are always missing.
Work out the real time now: with those segments added back, it reads 23:47.
23:47 + 3 h 45 min = 3:32 the next morning: 03:32.
Now remove the same two segments from 0, 3, 3, 2. That's picture A.
b2019-28.check: In A, each digit with the two segments put back gives 0 3 3 2. ✓
b2019-28.spot: Broken displays? First find the real numbers, then do the math.
b2019-28.oops: Adding time to the broken digits directly.

b2019-30.ask: Machines: 1 white → 4 red, or 1 red → 3 white. Zev starts with 4 white. After 11 exchanges he has 31 tokens. How many are red?
steps: White → 4 red: 1 token becomes 4, so +3 tokens. Red → 3 white: +2 tokens.
Start 4 tokens, end 31: that's 27 more from 11 exchanges.
If all 11 were +2: 22. We need 5 more, and each white→red exchange gives 1 more than a red→white. So 5 white→red and 6 red→white.
Red tokens: +4 for each of the 5 = 20, then −1 for each of the 6 = 14.
b2019-30.spot: Two kinds of swaps and a total? Pretend all were one kind, then count the extras.
b2019-30.oops: Forgetting each exchange also uses up a token.
